correctness.rationale: For each image line L there are h=q^(n−1) idempotents u_L f with f(u_L)=1. From each nonzero product the next image must avoid its kernel, giving survival a^(k−1). The trace is the cyclic product of k line-to-line evaluations. For equal adjacent lines the evaluation is 1; otherwise it is uniform over the field. The nonzero-evaluation transfer matrix q^(-1)I+(1−q^(-1))J has eigenvalues h and q^(-1) with multiplicities 1,N−1, giving nonzero trace mass C_k. Except when all lines coincide, conditional on nonzero trace the product includes a uniform nonzero scalar; the all-equal event has probability D_k and trace one. This gives the claimed bias, with q=2 vacuous. Since X²=tr(X)X in rank one, nilpotence and its index follow. Conjugacy is transitive within rank-one trace classes of sizes N(h−1) at zero and Nh per nonzero trace, giving the pointwise law. Relative to uniform after conditioning on survival, trace zero and each nonzero trace other than one are deficits (D_k>(N−1)b^k), and the trace-one excess is the claimed TV distance, including k=1 and q=2. Both packaged verifiers and their finite outputs were inspected, not executed.

evidence: Put h=q^(n−1), m=Nh, A=h^(2(k−1)), B=(h/q)^(k−1), Z=h^(k−1). The indexed zero fiber is m^k−mA. Its nonzero rank-one fiber is h(A−B)/(q^n−1)+1_{tr≠0}(B−Z)/(q−1)+1_{tr=1}Z.

Here A/m^(k−1)=a^(k−1), B/m^(k−1)=b^(k−1), Z/m^(k−1)=D_k, and 1−a=(N−1)b. Multiplying each nonzero-trace target probability by m gives class mass (C_k−D_k)/(q−1)+D_k·1_{tr=1}. Subtracting its sum from one gives total nilpotence; subtracting the zero mass then gives nonzero nilpotence.
After conditioning on survival, only trace one exceeds the uniform rank-one trace mass. The amount of its excess is [(N−1)b^k+(q−2)D_k]/[(q−1)a^(k−1)], the scalar TV formula.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The pointwise law, nilpotence and bias are direct normalization and summation. The TV formula is a mechanical consequence of the same class-resolved law and the elementary uniform orbit sizes, even if the earlier result does not display the identical scalar expression.
